name: Colorado Sunburst Anemone
description: A vibrant reef centerpiece featuring rich orange and golden tones with beautifully textured tentacles. The Colorado Sunburst Anemone brings striking color and movement to a well-established saltwater aquarium.

name: Ultra Goblin Goniopora
description: Bring your reef to life with the Ultra Goblin Goniopora , a luminous showpiece known for its intense green polyps and hypnotic movement. With its long, flower-like tentacles that pulse gently in the current, this coral offers a vibrant contrast that instantly elevates any aquascape. Under actinic lighting, its neon tones glow beautifully, making it a favorite among collectors. This particular frag is healthy, well-acclimated, and measures approximately. Each piece is unique, but all share that signature “goblin-green” brilliance that makes them stand out in any reef. Goniopora Coral Care Guide Origin Native to the Indo-Pacific region, Goniopora corals are commonly found in lagoon and reef slope habitats. Lighting Requirements Ultra Goblin Goniopora prefers moderate to high lighting. Too little light may cause fading, while too much can lead to stress. Start in a mid-light zone and adjust based on polyp extension. Low Light: 30–70 PAR Medium Light: 70–120 PAR High Light: 120–180 PAR Water Flow Gentle, indirect flow is ideal. Direct blasts from pumps may cause polyps to retract or become damaged. Feeding While Goniopora hosts zooxanthellae for photosynthesis, it benefits from target feeding. Use micro foods like reef roids, powdered coral blends, or phytoplankton once or twice a week to enhance growth and coloration. Placement Allow space for full polyp extension. Avoid placing it too close to aggressive corals. Ideal placement is on a flat rock ledge or sandbed platform where water movement is soft and steady. Acclimation Take your time when introducing this coral to your tank. Drip acclimation is recommended. Keep water parameters stable, as Goniopora can be sensitive to changes in alkalinity, salinity, and flow. Final Note Ultra Goblin Goniopora is perfect for hobbyists looking to add movement, color, and uniqueness to their reef. With proper care, it will reward you with graceful sway and show-stopping beauty.

name: Biscuit Stars
description: Add a touch of coastal charm to your reef with Biscuit Stars , named for their rounded, cushion-like shape and soft sandy coloration. These peaceful invertebrates bring a unique, natural presence to your aquarium floor and contribute to a healthy ecosystem by gently sifting through detritus and leftover food. Each specimen is about [insert size], hardy, and reef-safe—perfect for both beginner and experienced hobbyists seeking subtle movement and texture in their aquascape. Biscuit Star Care Guide Origin Commonly found in shallow coastal zones and sandy reef flats of the Indo-Pacific. Lighting Requirements Biscuit Stars do not rely on light and can thrive under any reef lighting condition. Water Flow Low to moderate flow is ideal. Too strong a current may limit their ability to move naturally across the sandbed. Feeding These stars are detritivores. They feed on decaying matter, uneaten food, and biofilm. In low-nutrient systems, offer occasional small bits of frozen food or sinking pellets. Placement Place directly on the sandbed. Avoid sharp rocks or aggressive tank mates that might disturb or injure them. Ideal for peaceful community tanks. Acclimation Biscuit Stars are sensitive to rapid changes in salinity. Drip acclimate slowly over 1–2 hours and avoid direct exposure to air during transfers. Final Note Low-maintenance, peaceful, and undeniably adorable, Biscuit Stars are a fantastic addition to any reef tank’s cleanup crew. Their subtle appearance adds visual diversity without overwhelming other display elements.

name: Saltwater Fish Food – Premium Blend (100g Pack)
description: Give your reef residents the nutrition they deserve with our Premium Saltwater Fish Food —a balanced, protein-rich formula designed to mimic natural ocean diets. Packed with high-quality ingredients like marine proteins, spirulina, krill, garlic, and essential vitamins , this blend enhances coloration, boosts immunity, and promotes healthy growth in both community and predator tanks. 🐟 Ideal For: Clownfish Tangs Wrasses Damsels Gobies Anthias Angelfish Butterflyfish 🌊 Why It Stands Out: ✅ Made from marine-based ingredients ✅ Boosts color, immunity, and appetite ✅ Doesn’t cloud water ✅ Fortified with omega-3 and garlic extract for digestion & disease resistance ✅ Suitable for daily feeding 🍽️ Feeding Directions: Feed small amounts 1–2 times daily. Only offer what your fish can consume within 2–3 minutes. Remove excess to maintain water quality. 📦 Available Forms: Granules (slow-sinking, perfect for mid-water feeders) Pellets (floating and sinking mix) Flakes (great for top-feeders) Freeze-dried options (mysis, krill, brine shrimp – sold separately) 🧊 Storage Tips: Keep in a cool, dry place. For maximum freshness, reseal the pouch after each use. Store in the fridge or freezer for long-term use. 🌈 Upgrade Your Feeding Routine Pair this food with Nori Sheets , Live Phyto , or Enriched Brine Shrimp for a complete marine diet plan.

name: Neon Raspberry Blast Ricordea
description: Bright. Bold. Bursting with color. The Neon Raspberry Blast Ricordea is a showstopping soft coral featuring a radiant raspberry base, fluorescent orange and green bubbles, and subtle blue accents that glow intensely under actinic light. Its compact size, textured surface, and vibrant pop make it perfect for nano tanks or as a color highlight in larger reefs. This WYSIWYG frag measures approximately ¾ to 1 inch and is fully aquacultured. 🧼 Ricordea Yuma Care Guide About Ricordea yuma Ricordea yuma is a unique corallimorph that combines the color of zoanthids with the texture of mushrooms. Known for its bubble-like tentacles and exotic appearance, this soft coral doesn’t have a stony skeleton, making it flexible and easy to place. Yumas can be sensitive at first, but once established, they’re hardy, long-lasting, and fast-growing. 🌍 Origin Aquacultured from Indo-Pacific strains, selectively grown for vivid, stable pigmentation and improved tank adaptability. 💡 Lighting Requirements Thrives under moderate to high light. Blues and actinics enhance its fluorescent tones dramatically. Low Light: 40–60 PAR Medium Light: 60–120 PAR High Light: 120–150+ PAR (with slow acclimation) 🌊 Water Flow Low to moderate flow. Too much flow can cause detachment or prevent full polyp inflation. A gentle, indirect current is ideal for maximum expansion and movement. 🍽️ Feeding Photosynthetic but will accept micro-feedings. Occasional spot feeding with reef roids, powdered coral foods, or phytoplankton can promote faster growth and brighter colors. 🌱 Propagation Easy to propagate once settled. Ricordea can split naturally or be fragged manually by experienced reefers. Always use coral-safe dips post-frag to prevent infection. 🔄 Acclimation Drip acclimate for 30–45 minutes. Avoid handling the oral disk directly, as Yuma tissue is delicate and prone to stress during transfer. ⚠️ Placement Tip: Place on rubble rock, frag tiles, or isolated spots in the sand to control spread. Avoid aggressive corals nearby, though Ricordea itself is non-aggressive. 🌈 Why It’s Special: The Neon Raspberry Blast morph combines hot pinks, neon oranges, and electric greens in a glowing, gem-like package. It’s a rare color combo and an absolute must-have for collectors who want serious pop under blues.

name: Cynarina Ultra
description: A true showpiece— Cynarina Ultra delivers jaw-dropping color and soft, hypnotic movement. With its oversized, jelly-like lobes and intense coloration—ranging from electric red and teal , to iridescent orange, pink, or metallic rainbow blends —this coral is a top-shelf addition to any luxury reef tank. This WYSIWYG specimen expands up to 5–6 inches when fully inflated and is aquacultured for resilience and longevity. 🧼 Cynarina Coral Care Guide About Cynarina lacrymalis Cynarina, also known as Cat’s Eye Coral , is a large polyp stony (LPS) coral loved for its massive fleshy body and transparent, bubble-like tissue. The Ultra grade represents the highest level of coloration and rarity—featuring exceptional contrast, clarity, and depth. It’s peaceful, easy to care for, and a magnet for attention in reef displays. 🌍 Origin Indo-Pacific origin, with this Ultra Grade piece sustainably aquacultured under controlled conditions. 💡 Lighting Requirements Low to moderate lighting is best to prevent bleaching and preserve the coral’s vibrant hues. Low Light: 30–60 PAR Medium Light: 60–90 PAR Best placed in shaded sandbed zones or lower rockwork. 🌊 Water Flow Low, indirect flow is ideal. Gentle current allows full expansion while preventing debris from settling in folds. Avoid strong, direct jets. 🍽️ Feeding While photosynthetic, Cynarina thrives with 2–3 targeted feedings per week. Offer mysis, reef roids, LPS pellets, or finely chopped seafood when feeder tentacles are visible (usually at night or during lights-off periods). 🌱 Propagation Not frag-friendly. Cynarina is a single-polyp coral and must be propagated by expert aquaculture facilities. Each specimen is unique and irreplaceable. 🔄 Acclimation Use a slow drip acclimation (45–60 minutes) to avoid shock. Keep calcium (400–450 ppm), alkalinity (8–10 dKH), and magnesium (1300–1400 ppm) stable for long-term success. ⚠️ Placement Tip: Place on a flat, soft sandbed away from aggressive neighbors or jagged rocks. This coral expands significantly and needs space to avoid injury. 🌈 Why It’s Ultra: Exceptional color saturation (not commonly seen in wild Cynarinas) Extreme tissue clarity and inflation Hand-selected for symmetry, contrast, and health If you're curating a collector’s reef, Cynarina Ultra is a must-have centerpiece.

name: Seaweed for Fish – 10 Sheets
description: Keep your herbivores healthy and vibrant with our Premium Seaweed Sheets —specially dried and packed for marine and freshwater aquarium fish. Each pack includes 10 ultra-fresh sheets of nutrient-rich nori , ideal for tangs, angelfish, rabbitfish, plecos, and other algae grazers. It’s a natural, protein-rich food source that enhances coloration, promotes digestion, and mimics their natural diet. 🌿 Product Highlights: 100% Natural Dried Seaweed (Nori) Pack includes 10 large, easy-to-tear sheets No preservatives or artificial additives High in vitamins, minerals, and marine protein Boosts immune system and natural coloration 🐟 Ideal For: Saltwater: Tangs, Foxface, Blennies, Angelfish, Wrasses Freshwater: Plecos, Mbuna, Goldfish, Koi 🍽️ Feeding Instructions: Clip 1/3 to 1/2 sheet to a seaweed feeder clip or secure with a rubber band to a rock. Place in tank and allow fish to graze. Remove uneaten seaweed after 4–6 hours to prevent water quality issues. Feed once daily or as needed depending on your tank’s algae grazers. 🧊 Storage Tip: Keep in a cool, dry place. Reseal after use to maintain freshness. 📦 Package Includes: 10 Full-Sized Dried Seaweed Sheets Resealable pouch for long-lasting use 🌟 Why It’s Special: Trusted by aquarists worldwide, this seaweed delivers clean energy and brilliant color to your herbivorous fish. A staple in any feeding rotation.

name: Open Brain Coral
description: Elegant and full of personality, the Open Brain Coral brings stunning color and gentle movement to your reef tank. With its meaty, ridged tissue and mesmerizing patterns in red, green, gold, and even rainbow morphs, this coral expands beautifully during the day and glows under actinic light. This WYSIWYG specimen spans 3–5 inches and is aquacultured for long-term success. 🧼 Open Brain Coral Care Guide About Trachyphyllia geoffroyi The Open Brain Coral is a large polyp stony (LPS) coral with a single, fleshy polyp over a skeletal base. Known for its undulating surface and vibrant coloration, it’s a peaceful coral that does best when given space to fully expand on a soft substrate. Suitable for both beginner and experienced reefers. 🌍 Origin Native to the Indo-Pacific, commonly found in shallow lagoons and sandy reef slopes. Most modern specimens are aquacultured. 💡 Lighting Requirements Thrives in low to moderate light. High-intensity lighting may cause fading or stress. Under blue LEDs, this coral often fluoresces brightly. Low Light: 30–60 PAR Medium Light: 60–100 PAR Ideal placement: bottom third of the tank, preferably on the sandbed. 🌊 Water Flow Low to moderate, indirect flow is ideal. This keeps the coral clean without irritating its fleshy tissue. Avoid direct jets or turbulent areas. 🍽️ Feeding Though it photosynthesizes, the Open Brain Coral appreciates target feeding 2–3 times per week. Use mysis, finely chopped seafood, or LPS-specific foods for best results. 🌱 Propagation Not typically fragged at home due to its single-polyp structure. Propagation should be done professionally via tissue regrowth or polyp splitting. 🔄 Acclimation Acclimate slowly (45–60 minutes drip method) to ensure the coral adjusts to salinity and temperature. Keep calcium, alkalinity, and magnesium levels stable. ⚠️ Placement Tip: Always place on soft substrate like sand, away from sharp rocks or aggressive corals. It inflates significantly and needs space to open fully without injury. 🌟 Why It’s Special: The Open Brain Coral adds a soft, flowing focal point to any reef, with stunning color variations and a peaceful temperament—perfect for reefers who want both beauty and balance.

name: Flat Open Brain Coral
description: Graceful, vibrant, and easy to love — the Flat Open Brain Coral , also known as Trachyphyllia , features a flat, disc-like profile with mesmerizing folds and bold color combinations. This WYSIWYG piece showcases radiant streaks of red, green, and metallic gold radiating from a central mouth, with soft fleshy tissue that sways gently in the current. It’s a perfect showpiece for beginners and collectors alike. 🧼 Trachyphyllia Coral Care Guide About Trachyphyllia geoffroyi Commonly called the Flat Open Brain Coral, this LPS coral is known for its rippling, fleshy surface and brilliant pigmentation. It’s a solitary polyp species with a round or slightly elongated shape that lies directly on the sandbed. Peaceful, hardy, and photosynthetic, it makes a fantastic centerpiece in any reef. 🌍 Origin Native to sandy lagoons and reef slopes across the Indo-Pacific. Most specimens available today are aquacultured or sustainably harvested. 💡 Lighting Requirements Prefers low to moderate lighting. Too much intensity can lead to bleaching or polyp retraction, while soft light enhances color vibrancy. Low Light: 30–60 PAR Medium Light: 60–100 PAR Best placement: on the sandbed with gentle, indirect lighting. 🌊 Water Flow Low, random flow is ideal. The coral should expand freely without being blasted by direct current, which can damage the soft tissue. 🍽️ Feeding Though primarily photosynthetic, Flat Brain Corals benefit greatly from regular feedings. Target-feed 2–3 times per week using mysis shrimp, LPS pellets, or reef roids for faster growth and deeper coloration. 🌱 Propagation Not suitable for casual fragging. Trachyphyllia is a single-polyp coral and propagation should only be performed by professionals using specialized aquaculture techniques. 🔄 Acclimation Use a slow drip acclimation over 45–60 minutes. Stability in salinity, calcium, and alkalinity is key to long-term success. ⚠️ Placement Tip: Place directly on the sandbed with no sharp rock contact. It inflates substantially and needs a soft, stable resting spot to avoid tearing. 🌈 Why It’s Special: With its wide, flat form and vibrant, marbled coloration , the Flat Open Brain Coral is an eye-catching, peaceful coral that plays beautifully with lighting and flow. A true gem for reefers who love both beauty and ease.

name: Blastomussa Orange with Yellow Rim
description: Bright, fiery, and unforgettable—this Orange Blastomussa with a radiant yellow center is a living ember in your reef. The plump, fleshy polyps radiate vibrant orange tones, accented by a glowing yellow mouth that shimmers under blue lighting. This WYSIWYG frag includes 3–5 healthy, aquacultured heads and is ready to light up any tank with warmth and motion. 🧼 Blastomussa Coral Care Guide About Blastomussa wellsi This species of Blastomussa is a prized large polyp stony (LPS) coral, known for its circular, fleshy polyps and mesmerizing color morphs. It’s ideal for both beginner reefers and experienced collectors due to its hardiness, peaceful nature, and low-maintenance requirements. The orange and yellow combo is less common and highly sought after for color-balanced aquascapes. 🌍 Origin Aquacultured from Indo-Pacific stock. Selectively grown for vivid pigmentation and robust polyp health. 💡 Lighting Requirements Low to moderate lighting helps preserve deep saturation and prevent bleaching. The yellow center glows beautifully under blues and actinics. Low Light: 30–60 PAR Medium Light: 60–100 PAR Best placement: lower to mid-levels of the tank, with gentle shade and indirect light. 🌊 Water Flow Low, indirect flow is best. Enough to keep detritus off but soft enough to let the coral fully inflate without irritation. 🍽️ Feeding While it thrives on photosynthesis, this coral loves target feeding. Feed 1–2 times a week with fine meaty foods—reef roids, powdered coral blends, or finely chopped mysis. Feeding enhances polyp expansion, growth, and color richness. 🌱 Propagation Once the colony develops multiple heads, it can be fragged easily with coral clippers or a diamond saw. Allow proper recovery in a low-stress area after fragging. 🔄 Acclimation Acclimate slowly over 30–45 minutes using a drip method. Stable alkalinity and moderate nutrient levels will ensure lasting health and color. ⚠️ Placement Tip: Peaceful and non-aggressive—Blastomussa can be placed near most corals. Allow space for inflation, as the polyps can swell significantly when happy. 🔥 Why It’s Special: The sunburst orange paired with a neon yellow center creates a vibrant, eye-catching contrast that stands out even among high-end coral displays. It’s the perfect accent piece for color-rich reef scapes or nano tanks.

name: Blastomussa Purple With Yellow Mouth
description: Compact in size, massive in impact—this Purple Blastomussa with a neon yellow mouth glows like a cosmic flower under reef lighting. Its fleshy, scalloped polyps display rich violet to deep grape tones, perfectly contrasted by the bright, glowing yellow oral disk. Ideal for nano tanks or adding a high-contrast pop to larger systems, this WYSIWYG frag features 3–5 fully encrusted, aquacultured heads. 🧼 Blastomussa Coral Care Guide About Blastomussa wellsi Blastomussa is a slow-growing large polyp stony (LPS) coral, known for its unique, soft-looking structure and vibrant color morphs. It’s one of the few corals that works well in both beginner setups and collector tanks. Peaceful and hardy, it expands fully under the right conditions and adds a soft pulse of color and texture to the reef. 🌍 Origin Aquacultured from Indo-Pacific lineage for increased coloration and survivability. This yellow-mouth morph is selectively grown and rarely found in the wild. 💡 Lighting Requirements Prefers lower to moderate light. Too much intensity may cause polyp retraction or color fading. Low Light: 30–60 PAR Medium Light: 60–100 PAR Ideal placement: mid-to-low areas of the tank, tucked into shaded rock crevices or coral islands. 🌊 Water Flow Low, indirect flow helps this coral open fully while preventing debris buildup. Strong or direct flow can prevent polyp inflation. 🍽️ Feeding While photosynthetic, this coral responds well to feeding. Target-feed 1–2 times per week using coral foods like Reef Roids, powdered blends, or micro-sized meaty foods to boost growth and vibrancy. 🌱 Propagation Easy to frag once the colony has multiple heads. Use a coral saw or bone cutters and allow healing in a low-stress, iodine-dipped recovery zone. 🔄 Acclimation Use a drip acclimation method over 30–45 minutes to minimize shock. Blastomussa prefers stable salinity, pH, and moderate nutrient levels. ⚠️ Placement Tip: Blastomussa is peaceful and can be placed near most corals without risk of aggression. Allow space for inflation to avoid crowding. 🌈 Why It’s Special: The vibrant yellow mouth creates a glowing focal point against the dark purple lobes , giving it a galactic, eye-like look that stands out under actinic blues. A must-have for any collector looking to build a palette of rare and vivid LPS corals.

name: Acantho Red With Yellow and Pink Mouth
description: Bold. Luminous. Rare. This Red Acanthophyllia with a sunburst yellow and blush pink mouth is a collector’s dream. Its vibrant red body radiates under reef lighting, while the contrasting multicolor mouth glows like a molten core—offering a centerpiece coral that looks alive with energy. Measuring 5–6 inches fully inflated, this WYSIWYG gem is a one-of-a-kind showpiece, aquacultured for long-term success. 🧼 Acanthophyllia Coral Care Guide About Acanthophyllia deshayesiana Known as the Donut Coral or Meat Coral , Acanthophyllia is a large single-polyp LPS coral with dramatic color combinations, ultra-fleshy texture, and peaceful temperament. It thrives on stability, slow growth, and regular feeding—making it a prized coral for mature reef systems. 🌍 Origin Aquacultured from premium Indo-Pacific strains. This rare tri-color mouth morph is not commonly seen in wild imports, offering uniqueness and resilience in one stunning coral. 💡 Lighting Requirements Low to moderate light is ideal to preserve color intensity and prevent tissue stress. Low Light: 30–60 PAR Medium Light: 60–90 PAR Best placed on the sandbed in a shaded or low-light section of the tank. 🌊 Water Flow Low, gentle flow keeps this coral inflated and thriving. High flow can tear soft tissue or prevent full expansion. 🍽️ Feeding Photosynthetic but benefits greatly from target feeding. Offer meaty foods like mysis, LPS pellets, or finely chopped clam 2–3 times a week, especially when feeder tentacles extend (usually at night). 🌱 Propagation Acanthophyllia is not a frag-friendly coral. Each specimen is a single-polyp masterpiece and must be handled with care. Best propagated by professional aquaculture. 🔄 Acclimation Use a slow drip method (60+ minutes) to avoid osmotic shock. Maintain high water quality with stable calcium, alkalinity, and magnesium levels. ⚠️ Tank Tip: Place on a smooth sandbed, away from rock edges or sharp frag plugs. This coral inflates dramatically and requires space to avoid damage and irritation. 🌟 Why It’s Special: This morph combines fiery red flesh with a yellow-pink gradient mouth —like a living gemstone under blues and whites. A perfect statement piece for luxury displays and serious reef collectors.

name: Bi Color Goniopora Yellow Mouth
description: Vibrant, exotic, and full of motion — this Bi-Color Goniopora flaunts a dazzling gradient of deep teal to soft lavender tentacles, all centered around a striking neon yellow mouth . It pulses rhythmically with every current, bringing dynamic life to your reefscape. This WYSIWYG aquacultured frag measures roughly 1 inch and is ideal for collectors or aquarists looking to elevate their coral game. 🧼 Goniopora Coral Care Guide About Goniopora spp. Goniopora, or Flowerpot Coral , is a beloved LPS known for its long, waving polyps that resemble a blooming field of flowers. Bi-color variants like this one are especially sought after due to their unique pigmentation and high visual impact in reef tanks. Though traditionally considered sensitive, modern aquacultured frags are significantly hardier and more forgiving. 🌍 Origin Aquacultured from Indo-Pacific lineages with selective propagation for rare coloration and improved resilience. 💡 Lighting Requirements Moderate lighting will bring out the best of both the bi-color gradient and the glowing yellow mouth. Avoid harsh direct lighting to preserve depth of color. Low Light: 40–70 PAR Medium Light: 70–120 PAR Ideal Placement: mid to lower tank zone with gentle indirect light. 🌊 Water Flow Gentle, indirect flow is key. Just enough to let the polyps sway and breathe without collapsing. Strong flow can damage the delicate tentacles or cause full retraction. 🍽️ Feeding Boost growth and intensity with regular feedings. Target-feed 2–3 times a week using powdered coral foods (Reef Roids, Benepets, Coral Dust) or live phytoplankton. 🌱 Propagation This Goniopora is aquacultured and fully healed. It can be fragged carefully once mature, though best left to experienced reefers due to skeletal density and soft polyp structure. 🔄 Acclimation Use a slow drip method for 45 minutes. Goniopora corals are sensitive to changes in salinity, alkalinity, and nutrient levels—stable parameters are critical. ⚠️ Reef Tip: Do not place near aggressive stinging corals. This beauty is peaceful and should be given space to open fully and flow with confidence. 🌈 Why It’s Special: The yellow mouth at the heart of this coral creates a glowing focal point, while the dual-tone tentacles create movement and color shift as light hits from different angles. A rare morph, perfect for high-end aquascapes or coral collectors.

name: Goniopora Purple Tentacles with Yellow Rim
description: Dazzling and hypnotic, this Goniopora boasts deep purple tentacles tipped with a vivid yellow rim , creating an electric contrast that shimmers under reef lighting. Often called the "Firework Goni" for its explosion of color and motion, this piece adds dynamic beauty and soft pulsing movement to any reef. Each WYSIWYG frag is roughly ¾–1 inch and fully aquacultured for improved hardiness. 🧼 Goniopora Coral Care Guide About Goniopora spp. Also known as Flowerpot Coral , Goniopora is a classic large polyp stony (LPS) coral famous for its daisy-like polyps and flowing motion. Once considered difficult to keep, aquacultured variants like this one are much more forgiving and thrive in stable systems with regular feeding and care. 🌍 Origin Indo-Pacific reefs, with this vibrant morph selectively grown in controlled aquaculture conditions. 💡 Lighting Requirements Moderate light works best. This Goniopora will glow under blues and fluorescents but may lose color or retract under excessive PAR. Low Light: 30–70 PAR Medium Light: 70–120 PAR Place mid-to-low in the tank with indirect light. 🌊 Water Flow Low to moderate, indirect flow is key. The tentacles should sway gently. Too much current may cause polyp retraction and stress. 🍽️ Feeding Thrives with routine feeding. Target-feed with micron-sized foods like Reef Roids, Coral Frenzy, or phytoplankton 2–3 times per week for extended polyp growth and vibrant color retention. 🌱 Propagation Goniopora can be fragged with care, though it's best done by experienced aquarists due to its skeletal base and delicate polyps. This specimen is already aquacultured and pre-healed. 🔄 Acclimation Drip acclimate for 30–45 minutes. Ensure stable alkalinity, calcium, and magnesium for long-term success. ⚠️ Placement Tip: Leave ample room between this and aggressive corals. Goniopora doesn’t sting but can be outcompeted. Keep in a peaceful zone with plenty of room to bloom. 🌟 Why It’s Special: The combination of royal purple tentacles and bright yellow rims makes this Goniopora a centerpiece coral. Rare and captivating—perfect for collectors or aquascapes needing a high-impact splash of motion and color.

name: Carpet Anemone
description: Massive, majestic, and mesmerizing—the Carpet Anemone is a living centerpiece that adds dramatic texture and color to any large reef setup. With its thick, velvety surface and vibrant tones of green, blue, purple, or tan, this anemone can reach up to 18 inches in diameter when fully grown. Its gently undulating surface mimics soft coral movement, while offering a natural home for clownfish species. 🧼 Carpet Anemone Care Guide About Stichodactyla spp. There are several species of Carpet Anemones, with the most popular in the hobby being Stichodactyla gigantea , S. haddoni , and S. mertensii . Each has slightly different care needs, but all are known for their broad, sticky oral discs and ability to host clownfish. They’re beautiful, but best suited for experienced reef keepers due to their size, stinging strength, and environmental sensitivity. 🌍 Origin Found across shallow sandy lagoons and reef flats throughout the Indo-Pacific region. 💡 Lighting Requirements Carpet anemones demand strong reef lighting. High PAR levels help maintain coloration, promote expansion, and support their photosynthetic zooxanthellae. Medium Light: 100–150 PAR High Light: 150–250+ PAR Provide bright, full-spectrum light similar to what you'd offer SPS corals. 🌊 Water Flow Moderate, random flow is preferred. Too much direct current can prevent it from settling, while too little may cause waste to collect. Allow it to find a calm but oxygenated area. 🍽️ Feeding Carpet Anemones are both photosynthetic and predatory. Offer meaty foods (silversides, shrimp, scallops, or high-quality pellets) once or twice a week. Avoid overfeeding to reduce waste buildup. 🐠 Clownfish Compatibility Pairs well with many clownfish species (especially Amphiprion clarkii , A. ocellaris , and A. percula ). Hosting behavior may take time but is often natural and rewarding to observe. ⚠️ Tank Requirements: Tank size: 75 gallons minimum (preferably larger) Mature system: 6+ months old with stable parameters Sandbed or flat rock: Allow it to settle where it chooses Lid recommended: Anemones can move, especially in early days 🔄 Acclimation Use a slow drip acclimation method (45–60 minutes minimum). Ensure stable temp (77–80°F), salinity (1.025), and strong oxygenation. ⚠️ Warning: The tentacles of Carpet Anemones are sticky and possess a potent sting—avoid placing near other corals or prized fish species that could be injured or eaten. Handle with gloves or a container, never bare hands. 🌈 Why It’s Special: A hosting anemone with bold presence, rich texture, and real movement— Carpet Anemones are the crown of naturalistic reef displays.

name: Purple with gold mouth
description: A true centerpiece with royal elegance—this Purple Acanthophyllia features a deep, velvety purple body contrasted by a radiant metallic gold mouth , making it one of the most stunning and rare color morphs available. The fleshy tissue ripples with iridescent undertones, glowing beautifully under both daylight and blues. This WYSIWYG specimen inflates to 5–6 inches and is fully aquacultured under stable conditions. 🧼 Acanthophyllia Coral Care Guide About Acanthophyllia deshayesiana Also known as the Donut Coral or Meat Coral , Acanthophyllia is a premium single-polyp LPS coral known for its massive size, peaceful nature, and vivid coloration. Its slow growth and rarity make it a prized coral for show tanks and serious collectors. 🌍 Origin Sustainably aquacultured from Indo-Pacific stock. This gold-mouth variant is highly sought after and uncommon in the wild trade. 💡 Lighting Requirements Low to moderate light is best. Too much light can stress or bleach the coral. Place in a shaded sandbed zone and acclimate slowly if moving to brighter areas. Low Light: 30–60 PAR Medium Light: 60–100 PAR Avoid intense direct LED or halide exposure. 🌊 Water Flow Low, gentle flow is ideal. The coral's soft, fleshy tissue expands best in calm conditions. Avoid strong currents that can lead to retraction or damage. 🍽️ Feeding Acanthophyllia will extend feeder tentacles primarily at night. Target-feed 2–3 times per week with chunky meaty foods (mysis, krill, clam, reef blend) to promote fullness, coloration, and long-term health. 🌱 Propagation Not frag-friendly. Being a single-polyp species, it can only be propagated through specialized aquaculture methods. Each one is truly one of a kind. 🔄 Acclimation Use a slow 60-minute drip acclimation. This coral is sensitive to sudden changes in salinity, pH, or temperature—stable parameters are crucial. ⚠️ Placement Tip: Place on a soft sandbed, away from rough rock edges or aggressive corals. It inflates significantly and needs space to prevent damage or crowding. 🌟 Why It’s Special: The Gold Mouth paired with royal purple flesh makes this piece an absolute standout. Rare, vibrant, and regal—perfect for hobbyists who want something no one else has.

name: Acanthophyllia
description: The crown jewel of LPS— Acanthophyllia is a showstopper in every reef it graces. With its massive fleshy body, mesmerizing swirl patterns, and deep, radiant colors ranging from blood red and electric green to watermelon and tie-dye blends, this coral is made to impress. This WYSIWYG specimen spans approximately 4–6 inches when fully inflated and is aquacultured for superior health and adaptation. 🧼 Acanthophyllia Coral Care Guide About Acanthophyllia deshayesiana Commonly known as the Meat Coral , Donut Coral , or Button Coral , Acanthophyllia is a large single-polyp LPS coral prized for its bold colors and incredible inflation. It's peaceful, hardy, and thrives in stable, mature reef systems. Its slow growth and stunning visual appeal make it a collector's must-have. 🌍 Origin Native to sandy reef floors and gentle slopes throughout the Indo-Pacific. This coral is now widely aquacultured due to high demand and environmental protections. 💡 Lighting Requirements Prefers lower to moderate light. High-intensity lighting may cause retraction or tissue stress. Start in a shaded zone and adjust slowly if needed. Low Light: 30–60 PAR Medium Light: 60–100 PAR Best placement: shaded areas of the sandbed or low ledges. 🌊 Water Flow Low, indirect flow is ideal. This allows the coral to expand fully without the risk of tissue damage. Excessive flow can cause deflation and irritation. 🍽️ Feeding Though photosynthetic, Acanthophyllia greatly benefits from target feeding 2–3 times a week. Offer chunky meaty foods—like mysis, krill, or clam bits—at night or when its feeder tentacles are extended. 🌱 Propagation Acanthophyllia is a single-polyp coral and cannot be fragged in the traditional sense. Propagation is done through careful natural reproduction in aquaculture systems. 🔄 Acclimation Use a slow drip acclimation process over 60 minutes. This coral is sensitive to swings in salinity, temperature, and pH—so consistency is key. ⚠️ Placement Tip: Place on a soft sandbed away from sharp rock edges. This coral inflates significantly and can be damaged by rough surfaces. Keep it isolated from aggressive neighbors. 🌈 Why It’s Special: Each Acanthophyllia is a one-of-a-kind masterpiece. No two look alike—making it not just a coral, but a true living gem in your reef.

name: Red Mouth with Yellow Tip Elegance Coral
description: Rare. Radiant. Regal. The Red Mouth with Yellow Tip Elegance Coral is a true collector’s gem. Featuring a deep, ruby-red central mouth surrounded by long, flowing tentacles tipped in glowing yellow, this coral brings bold contrast and captivating movement to your reef. Measuring 3–5 inches fully expanded, this WYSIWYG specimen is aquacultured, healthy, and ready to steal the spotlight in your tank. 🧼 Elegance Coral Care Guide About Catalaphyllia jardinei Elegance Corals are iconic LPS corals known for their fleshy tentacles and dynamic presence. This particular morph—highlighted by its rich red oral disk and bright yellow tips—is highly sought after for its exotic look and powerful visual punch. With the right placement and conditions, it thrives beautifully and lives up to its name. 🌍 Origin Originally native to sandy lagoons and reef slopes in the Indo-Pacific, this variety is aquacultured for improved resilience in home aquariums. 💡 Lighting Requirements Moderate lighting is preferred. High-intensity lighting can lead to tissue stress or bleaching. Place in a shaded or low-light zone and gradually adjust to stronger light if needed. Low Light: 30–60 PAR Medium Light: 60–100 PAR Position on the sandbed or low rock ledge for best results. 🌊 Water Flow Low to moderate, indirect flow helps the tentacles stay inflated and gently swaying. Avoid high flow areas that may flatten or damage the soft tissue. 🍽️ Feeding Although photosynthetic, this coral appreciates regular target feeding. Offer meaty foods such as mysis, chopped shrimp, or LPS pellets 2–3 times a week to promote health and vibrant expansion. 🌱 Propagation Due to its single-polyp nature and delicate tissue, Elegance Coral is not typically fragged in home aquariums. Best propagated by professionals through careful aquaculture practices. 🔄 Acclimation Elegance Corals are sensitive to sudden changes—use a slow drip method over 45–60 minutes. Place in a quiet, stable section of the tank during initial acclimation. ⚠️ Tank Tip: Elegance Corals expand significantly—ensure ample space between it and neighboring corals to prevent stinging. A sandy bottom with minimal rock contact is ideal. 🔥 Why It’s Special: The Red Mouth with Yellow Tip variation is a rare morph with powerful contrast—combining the intensity of deep red with the glow of golden tentacle tips. It’s not just a coral, it’s a statement.

name: Blastomussa Coral
description: Compact, colorful, and full of charm—the Blastomussa Coral is a must-have for LPS lovers. With its fleshy, flower-like polyps and vibrant ringed patterns in red, green, teal, or neon orange, this coral adds a burst of color to even the smallest spaces in your reef. This WYSIWYG frag includes 3–5 plump, healthy polyps grown under stable aquaculture conditions. 🧼 Blastomussa Coral Care Guide About Blastomussa wellsi Blastomussa is a stunning large polyp stony coral, known for its soft, inflated polyps and easygoing nature. It grows in a dome-like cluster, resembling mini anemones, and stays relatively compact—perfect for nano tanks or filling color gaps in larger setups. A great choice for beginners and experienced reefers alike. 🌍 Origin Naturally found in the Indo-Pacific, often in deeper, lower-light reef zones. This piece has been aquacultured for enhanced coloration and long-term tank performance. 💡 Lighting Requirements Thrives in low to moderate lighting. Higher light may cause color shift or polyp retraction, so avoid placing it under intense LEDs without shade or diffusion. Low Light: 30–60 PAR Medium Light: 60–100 PAR Ideal placement: mid-to-low tank zones, on rocks or substrate with room to expand. 🌊 Water Flow Low to moderate flow is best. Gentle movement helps keep the coral clean while allowing its polyps to remain fully inflated and open. 🍽️ Feeding While Blastomussa is photosynthetic, it will eagerly accept occasional feedings of mysis, brine shrimp, or reef roids. Feed 1–2 times a week to support growth and vivid coloration. 🌱 Propagation Blastomussa can be fragged once colonies form multiple heads. Each head can grow into a new polyp with proper care and healing time. 🔄 Acclimation Standard slow drip acclimation (30–45 minutes) is recommended. Like all LPS, it prefers stability—avoid sudden parameter swings for best health. ⚠️ Placement Tip: Blastomussa is peaceful and won’t send out stinging tentacles, making it a great neighbor for other corals. Still, leave a bit of room to allow full inflation and growth. 🌈 Color Morphs Available (upon request): Blood Red with Neon Green Centers Rainbow Blastos Toxic Teal Deepwater Purple Glow

name: Electric red tip Elegance
description: Electrify your reef with the Electric Red Tip Elegance Coral —a true centerpiece coral with dramatic color and flow. This specimen boasts long, fleshy tentacles in shimmering neon green or cream, tipped with vivid electric red or magenta hues that pulse and sway with the current. Measuring approximately 3–4 inches when fully extended, this WYSIWYG coral is bold, elegant, and hard to ignore. 🧼 Elegance Coral Care Guide About Catalaphyllia jardinei The Elegance Coral is a large polyp stony (LPS) coral known for its ribbon-like tentacles, often forming a crown-like display. While once considered delicate, aquacultured specimens—especially those with bright red tips—have proven more adaptable and long-lasting in home aquariums. It’s ideal for reefers with moderate experience looking to elevate their tank’s aesthetic. 🌍 Origin Originally found in sandy lagoons and reef slopes in the Indo-Pacific, this variety is aquacultured to ensure better hardiness and adaptability. 💡 Lighting Requirements Prefers moderate lighting. High PAR levels can stress the coral, while too little light may dull its color and inhibit expansion. Low Light: 30–60 PAR Medium Light: 60–100 PAR Place on the substrate or low rock ledge with diffuse lighting for best display. 🌊 Water Flow Low to moderate, indirect flow is essential. Too much current will prevent the coral from fully extending and can cause tissue damage. 🍽️ Feeding Although it's photosynthetic, regular target feeding enhances growth and vibrancy. Feed 2–3 times per week with chopped meaty foods like mysis, krill, or reef blends. 🌱 Propagation Elegance Corals are not typically fragged due to their single-polyp structure and soft tissue. Propagation is best left to specialized aquaculture operations. 🔄 Acclimation Use a slow drip acclimation (at least 45–60 minutes) and ensure stable parameters before introduction. Elegance Corals can be sensitive to sudden changes in salinity and pH. ⚠️ Placement Tip: This coral expands significantly—give it room! Keep away from aggressive stinging corals and consider a sandbed placement for natural expansion and cushion. 👑 Why It Stands Out: The Electric Red Tip variety is rare and highly sought after—its contrasting colors and graceful movement make it an eye-catching feature in any reef setup.

name: Tiger torch with cotton candy torch
description: Double the fire, double the flair. This Tiger Torch + Cotton Candy Torch coral combo brings high-end Euphyllia beauty straight to your reef. With the bold, striped golden flames of the Tiger Torch and the dreamy pastel pinks and minty tips of the Cotton Candy Torch, this pairing is perfect for hobbyists seeking movement, color contrast, and rare collectible pieces. Each frag in this duo includes 1–2 fully aquacultured heads. WYSIWYG – what you see is what you get. 🧼 Torch Coral Care Guide About Euphyllia glabrescens Torches are the royalty of LPS corals. Known for their dramatic, flowing tentacles and brilliant coloration, these corals bring both motion and intensity to reef tanks. While the Tiger Torch flaunts tiger-striped tentacles with neon tips, the Cotton Candy variant shines with a soft pastel palette that’s rare and highly prized in the hobby. 🌍 Origin Indo-Pacific reefs, with aquacultured lineage for improved hardiness and coloration. 💡 Lighting Requirements Moderate to high lighting is ideal. Both varieties will glow under blues and benefit from slow acclimation to stronger light. Low Light: 60–80 PAR Medium Light: 80–150 PAR High Light: 150–200 PAR (only with proper acclimation) 🌊 Water Flow Moderate, indirect flow. Torch tentacles should sway gently—too much flow may cause retraction or tissue damage. 🍽️ Feeding While they’re photosynthetic, these torches love occasional meaty treats. Target-feed small amounts of mysis, brine, or reef-specific blends 1–2 times a week for maximum growth and color pop. 🌱 Propagation Euphyllia torches grow via branching skeletal heads. Frag with care using coral cutters and allow healing in a low-flow, iodine-treated dip if needed. 🔄 Acclimation Essential for high-end LPS. Use a slow drip acclimation (45–60 minutes) and avoid sudden shifts in lighting or flow. Let them expand before adjusting placement. ⚠️ Space Required: Torch corals have long sweeper tentacles that can extend up to 6 inches or more. Keep a safe buffer zone between them and other corals to prevent stinging. 🔥 Collector’s Tip: Place them together in a low-to-mid tank zone with soft flow and LED blues for stunning nighttime fluorescence. The color contrast is absolutely jaw-dropping.

name: Cynaria Ultra
description: Make a bold statement in your reef with the ultra-fleshy and luminous Cynarina Coral . Known for its oversized, translucent bubble-like tissue and radiant coloration—from glowing pinks and reds to metallic greens and oranges—this coral is a true showstopper. Measuring 2–3 inches when inflated, this WYSIWYG piece adds a luxurious, soft-flowing texture to your reef tank. 🧼 Cynarina Coral Care Guide About Cynarina lacrymalis Often referred to as Cat’s Eye Coral or simply Cynaria , this large polyp stony (LPS) coral is prized for its jelly-like appearance and vibrant hues. It has a single, large central mouth and inflates significantly under the right conditions. While visually dramatic, it’s generally peaceful and moderately easy to care for with the proper environment. 🌍 Origin Native to sandy reef slopes and rubble zones of the Indo-Pacific, often found partially buried in substrate. 💡 Lighting Requirements Cynarina prefers low to moderate lighting. Too much intensity can cause tissue retraction or bleaching. Start in a shaded area and acclimate slowly. Low Light: 30–60 PAR Medium Light: 60–100 PAR Avoid placing under direct LEDs without diffusion. 🌊 Water Flow Low, indirect flow is best. High flow may damage its soft tissue or prevent full inflation. A calm zone will allow it to expand fully and show off its mesmerizing translucency. 🍽️ Feeding Cynarina benefits from regular target feeding. Offer small meaty foods like mysis shrimp, reef roids, or enriched brine shrimp 1–2 times per week to support health, growth, and coloration. 🌱 Propagation Fragging Cynarina is possible but challenging and not commonly done due to its single-polyp structure. Best left to expert hobbyists or professional aquaculture facilities. 🔄 Acclimation Acclimate carefully using a drip method over 45–60 minutes. Place on the sandbed or a stable, low-flow surface where it won’t be irritated by neighboring corals or high water movement. ⚠️ Placement Tip: This coral can inflate significantly—leave room around it to avoid contact with stinging corals or rockwork. Ideal for display tanks or low-competition LPS zones.

name: Daisy Coral
description: Delicate, unique, and full of charm— Daisy Coral adds soft floral movement to your reefscape. With its dainty, flower-shaped polyps and soft lavender or beige hues, this encrusting soft coral grows in low, bushy clusters that sway gently with the flow. It’s perfect for adding natural elegance to rockwork or filling in empty zones with subtle motion and texture. 🧼 Daisy Coral Care Guide About Knopia / Clavularia spp. Commonly referred to as Daisy Coral, this fast-growing soft coral resembles tiny daisies blooming across your rockwork. Unlike hard corals, it lacks a calcium skeleton, making it more flexible and forgiving—an excellent choice for beginner to intermediate hobbyists. Some variants may be labeled under Clavularia due to close visual similarities. 🌍 Origin Naturally found in shallow reef flats and lagoons across the Indo-Pacific region. 💡 Lighting Requirements Daisy Coral thrives under moderate lighting, though it’s quite adaptable. It glows beautifully under blues and doesn’t require intense PAR levels. Low Light: 30–70 PAR Medium Light: 70–120 PAR Great for mid to lower areas of the tank or to fill shadowed nooks. 🌊 Water Flow Moderate, random flow is ideal. Enough to keep detritus from settling while allowing polyps to sway gently. Too much flow can cause retraction, while too little may invite algae buildup. 🍽️ Feeding Photosynthetic and low-maintenance, Daisy Coral doesn’t require feeding, but it may benefit from occasional broadcast feeding with phytoplankton or amino acid blends for improved coloration and polyp extension. 🌱 Propagation Extremely easy to frag! Daisy Coral spreads via encrusting mat-like tissue and can be gently cut or peeled from rock to create new colonies. 🔄 Acclimation As with all corals, acclimate slowly using a drip method over 30–45 minutes. Place it in a low-light area initially, then move as needed based on response. ⚠️ Pro Tip: Daisy Coral grows quickly! It can overtake neighboring corals if not pruned or managed, so keep it in its own zone or on an isolated rock island.

name: Turban Snail
description: Meet your reef tank’s cleanup crew MVP—the Turban Snail . With its thick, beautifully spiraled shell and tireless appetite for algae, this hardy snail is a must-have for maintaining a pristine aquarium. It’s peaceful, reef-safe, and constantly on the move, scrubbing live rock, glass, and substrate alike. 🧼 Turban Snail Care Guide About Turbo Snails Named for their distinctive turban-shaped shells, these snails are part of the Turbo genus and are natural algae grazers. They’re extremely efficient at removing hair algae, film algae, and diatoms—making them one of the best utility inverts for reef keepers. They're hardy, low-maintenance, and perfect for reefers of all levels. 🌍 Origin Native to intertidal and reef zones throughout the Indo-Pacific region, including the Philippines and Fiji. 💡 Lighting Requirements Turban snails have no specific lighting needs. They’ll thrive under any standard reef tank lighting used to support corals or live rock. 🌊 Water Flow Adaptable to a range of flow conditions, but prefer moderate to strong flow zones where algae tends to grow. Make sure they can reach algae-covered surfaces safely. 🍽️ Feeding These snails are natural grazers and will eat algae off rocks, glass, and even equipment. If algae becomes scarce, supplement their diet with algae wafers or dried seaweed (nori). 🧠 Behavior & Compatibility Completely reef-safe Peaceful with all fish, inverts, and corals May accidentally knock over loosely placed frags or small decorations due to their size and strength—secure items properly 🔄 Acclimation Turban snails are sensitive to salinity changes. Use a drip acclimation method over 45–60 minutes for a smooth transition. Avoid exposing them to air during transfer—they can seal their operculum but prefer to stay submerged. ⚠️ Pro Tip: Always place them upright in the tank. If they fall on their back, they may struggle to flip over, especially on flat surfaces—give them a hand when needed!

name: Cat Eye Bubble Coral
description: Turn heads in your reef tank with the mesmerizing Cat Eye Bubble Coral . Featuring large, pearl-like vesicles with a subtle cat-eye glow and delicate iridescence, this coral adds both elegance and intrigue to any aquascape. This WYSIWYG specimen is approximately 2–3 inches when fully inflated and has been aquacultured under stable reef conditions. 🧼 Cat Eye Bubble Coral Care Guide About Plerogyra sinuosa The Cat Eye Bubble Coral is a variety of bubble coral known for its oversized, fluid-like bubbles that resemble translucent marbles with faint stripes—like a cat's eye. A peaceful and hardy LPS coral, it's a favorite for beginners and seasoned reefers alike. 🌍 Origin Found in the calm lagoon zones and reef slopes of the Indo-Pacific, particularly in sheltered, low-light areas. 💡 Lighting Requirements Prefers lower to moderate light levels. Too much light can cause the bubbles to deflate and stress the coral. Avoid direct exposure to high-intensity LEDs or metal halides. Low Light: 30–70 PAR Medium Light: 70–100 PAR Place in shaded or lower zones of the tank with slow acclimation if upgrading lighting. 🌊 Water Flow Low to moderate, indirect flow is ideal. The vesicles (bubbles) are delicate and can be torn by strong currents. A calm zone will help it inflate fully and show off its unique texture. 🍽️ Feeding Although it contains photosynthetic zooxanthellae, the Cat Eye Bubble Coral thrives with weekly feedings of small meaty foods—mysis, brine shrimp, or reef-specific blends. Target feeding helps growth and polyp extension. 🌱 Propagation Can be fragged by experienced aquarists, although it has a hard skeleton and delicate tissue. Proper healing and coral dips are essential after fragging. 🔄 Acclimation Use a slow drip method to match salinity and temperature. Bubble corals are sensitive to sudden changes and physical damage—handle with care during placement. ⚠️ Placement Tip: Keep a buffer zone! Bubble corals have long sweeper tentacles that can extend several inches at night, so give them space to avoid stinging nearby corals.

name: Skunk Cleaner Shrimp (Lysmata amboinensis)
description: Add a burst of personality and purpose to your reef with the Skunk Cleaner Shrimp. With its striking red and white racing stripe and elegant translucent legs, this little invert is more than just a pretty face—it's a reef janitor with attitude. Known for its peaceful nature and cleaning behavior, this shrimp will even set up cleaning stations for your fish. Each specimen is healthy, active, and reef-safe. 🧼 Skunk Cleaner Shrimp Care Guide About Lysmata amboinensis The Skunk Cleaner Shrimp is a beloved staple in the saltwater aquarium hobby. Recognized for its bold coloration and fascinating cleaning rituals, it will often climb on fish to remove parasites and dead tissue—earning its reputation as nature’s spa therapist. It’s peaceful, hardy, and thrives in community reef tanks. 🌍 Origin Native to the warm reef waters of the Indo-Pacific, including the Red Sea. 💡 Lighting Requirements No specific lighting requirements. The shrimp will adapt to your tank's existing reef lighting, often hiding under ledges or rockwork during acclimation. 🌊 Water Flow Moderate flow is ideal. The Skunk Cleaner likes areas where detritus can settle but won't mind active spots if enough rock cover is available. 🍽️ Feeding While it helps clean up leftover food and detritus, supplemental feeding is key to a healthy shrimp. Offer finely chopped meaty foods, sinking pellets, or freeze-dried plankton. Feed once daily or every other day depending on tank size and bioload. 🤝 Behavior & Compatibility Completely reef-safe Peaceful with fish, corals, and other inverts May be territorial toward its own kind unless introduced as a mated pair or small group Known to interact with fish for cleaning—especially tangs, wrasses, and gobies 🔄 Acclimation Proper drip acclimation is essential—shrimp are sensitive to rapid changes in salinity and temperature. Take your time with at least 45–60 minutes of slow acclimation before introducing it into the display tank. ⚠️ Pro Tip: Avoid housing with aggressive wrasses or predatory fish like large hawkfish or triggers that may see shrimp as a snack.

name: Branching Banana Hammer
description: Bring bold, tropical vibes to your reef with the Branching Banana Hammer Coral. With its bright yellow-green "banana" colored hammer-shaped tips and elegant branching skeleton, this piece adds both movement and vibrant contrast to any aquascape. This frag features 1–2 healthy, aquacultured heads and is WYSIWYG—what you see is exactly what you'll receive. 🧼 Branching Banana Hammer Care Guide About Euphyllia ancora The Banana Hammer is a variety of Euphyllia ancora, part of the hammer coral family, known for its chunky, hammer-shaped tentacles and branching growth form. It's relatively hardy and suitable for reefers with at least basic experience in LPS coral care. 🌍 Origin Native to the Indo-Pacific region, with aquacultured variants now thriving in sustainable farm environments. 💡 Lighting Requirements Banana Hammers enjoy moderate lighting. Too much direct intensity can bleach their tissue, while too little may cause retraction and dull coloration. Low Light: 40–70 PAR Medium Light: 70–120 PAR Place mid to lower in your tank and slowly acclimate to your lighting setup. 🌊 Water Flow Aim for gentle to moderate flow. The polyps should sway naturally—avoid strong currents that could cause the tissue to retract or tear. 🍽️ Feeding Although they receive energy from symbiotic zooxanthellae, occasional feedings with small meaty foods (mysis, brine shrimp, reef roids) will support better growth and coloration. Target-feed 1–2 times per week. 🌱 Propagation Thanks to its branching skeleton, the Banana Hammer is easy to frag with the right tools. Each branch can grow into a new colony if fragged properly and given time to recover. 🔄 Acclimation Handle with care and follow our Acclimation Guide before placing in your display tank. Euphyllia corals can be sensitive to rapid changes in light or water parameters. ⚠️ Note: Like most Euphyllia, the Banana Hammer has sweeper tentacles that can sting neighboring corals—give it some personal space in your reef layout!

name: Goniopora garden
description: Bring your reef to life with the elegant sway of this Blossoming Pink Goniopora Coral. Radiating delicate hues of pink and soft lavender, each polyp dances in the current like underwater petals. This WYSIWYG frag has been tank-raised for over a year and measures approximately 1 inch across when fully extended. 🧼 Goniopora Coral Care Guide About Goniopora Also known as “Flowerpot Coral,” Goniopora is a mesmerizing large polyp stony (LPS) coral. It's beloved for its long, flowing tentacles and daisy-like appearance. While stunning, it’s slightly more demanding than other LPS corals, making it best suited for reefers with intermediate experience. 🌍 Origin Native to shallow reef lagoons and turbid waters across the Indo-Pacific and Red Sea. 💡 Lighting Requirements Goniopora prefers moderate lighting, mimicking the scattered sunlight of its natural habitat. Overexposure can stress it, while too little light may inhibit growth. Low Light: 30–80 PAR Medium Light: 80–150 PAR Avoid placing under intense direct light without proper acclimation. 🌊 Water Flow A gentle, indirect flow is ideal. The tentacles should sway freely without being blasted. Too much flow may cause the polyps to stay retracted, reducing their feeding and overall health. 🍽️ Feeding Although it hosts zooxanthellae, supplemental feeding is highly encouraged. Feed it small particle foods like reef roids, phytoplankton, or finely chopped meaty foods 2–3 times a week for best results and long-term health. 🌱 Propagation Goniopora can be fragged, but it requires careful handling due to its skeletal structure and sensitivity. Most propagation is done by experienced reefers or aquaculture professionals. 🔄 Acclimation Goniopora is particularly sensitive to sudden changes. We strongly recommend following our Acclimation Guide to ensure a stress-free introduction to your reef environment.

name: Raspberry Neon Blast Ricordea Mushroom
description: Add a splash of color to your reef with this stunning Raspberry Neon Blast Ricordea Mushroom . It features a Purple and green center surrounded by a striking purple rim—truly a standout piece. This particular frag has been growing on our farm for nearly two years and measures approximately ¾ of an inch. What you see is exactly what you get (WYSIWYG). 🧼 Raspberry Neon Blast Ricordea Mushroom Care Guide About Ricordea Mushroom Originating from the Indo-Pacific region, Ricordea yuma is a unique species of corallimorph with a textured surface covered in small, bubble-like tentacles. These mushrooms are known for their bold colors and exotic look. However, they can be a bit temperamental, so we recommend them for hobbyists with some reef-keeping experience. 🌍 Origin These corals are commonly found throughout the vibrant reefs of the Indo-Pacific. 💡 Lighting Requirements Ricordea yuma tends to thrive under more intense lighting compared to its Caribbean counterparts. Aim to place them in areas of moderate to high light in your tank setup. Low Light: 30–50 PAR Medium Light: 50–150 PAR High Light: 150+ PAR For a more detailed understanding of reef lighting, feel free to explore our in-depth lighting guide. 🌊 Water Flow Yuma mushrooms prefer a calm environment. Place them in low-flow areas of your reef tank to avoid stress. Excessive flow can cause them to retract or even get dislodged and move around the tank. 🍽️ Feeding While Ricordea mushrooms rely mostly on their symbiotic zooxanthellae for energy, they also appreciate occasional feedings. Offer them tiny bits of food—like mysis or other fine meaty options—for added nutrition and better growth. 🌱 Propagation These mushrooms are great candidates for aquaculture. They’ve been successfully propagated in captivity, and with time and care, they can form part of a sustainable reef-keeping practice. 🔄 Acclimation Because shipping can stress marine animals, proper acclimation is crucial. Please follow our Acclimation Guide to give your Ricordea the smoothest transition into its new home.
